seed_ledger.name: Altamont Green River Pipeline Project
seed_ledger.reason: The project is a gathering line of about 43 miles and 20 inches carrying Uinta Basin gas to the Chipeta processing plant. It went into service in September 2025. Kinder Morgan says it relieves production constraints and cuts flaring. No source ties it to a data center or power plant. Searches turned up Crusoe flare-gas units in the basin from 2023, which are a different project. Searches run: 9. Sources checked: Kinder Morgan second-quarter 2024 and third-quarter 2025 earnings releases (project scope, in-service date); Western Midstream 2025 annual report (Chipeta interconnect finished, 150 MMcf/d); a Bureau of Land Management press release on the Chipeta slug catcher line (flaring and trucking reduction); Utah Public Service Commission docket index (safety filings only); Uinta Basin data center and gas power searches (nothing tied); Kinder Morgan data center commentary (no Utah Uinta tie).

evidence.note: Placed in service September 2025, relieves Uinta Basin constraints.
43 miles, 20 inch, 150 MMcf/d to Western Chipeta plant.
Chipeta interconnect for up to 150 MMcf/d completed in 2025.
Purpose is flaring reduction in the Altamont and Bluebell area.

candidates.name: Aquila Pipeline (Eagle Mountain)
candidates.researcher_notes: No existing row matches. The nearby Utah rows are the MountainWest Goshen expansions and the Magnum storage header line, which are different lines. Williams spring 2026 shipper board slides describe a 19 mile service pipeline from MountainWest to the Aquila power plant at Eagle Mountain, Utah. A Utah Public Service Commission notice from November 2025 says Will-Power UT LLC, owned by Williams, will build and own a 20 mile service pipeline to the plant and is still acquiring permits. The Williams customer meeting slides from March 2026 give a 12.5 year agreement and in-service dates in the second half of 2027 and first half of 2028. Length is staged as 19 miles from the Williams slides; the commission notice says about 20. Status is proposed because permits were still being acquired. Proposal year is the year of the commission notice. DataCenter is left blank. A local article ties the plant to the Meta campus, but it does not name the pipeline, and the commission notice only says the customer's industrial property. No route was found. The Williams slides also show a 1 mile service pipeline from Kern River to the plant. It has no source beyond the slides and no data center tie, and it is under 25 km, so it should not get its own row for now. Williams slides give no pipe diameter, capacity or cost. Confidence is medium: two Williams documents plus a state regulator filing, but the Williams documents come from one company. [QC] independent=yes claimed on 6 surviving ref(s) from 0 publisher(s) -> no.
